Gateway Condition Spotlight

For Newly Diagnosed Hypertension, Immediate Intervention Creates the Most Value

Deloitte’s research on gateway diseases, including hypertension, prediabetes, and obesity, finds that every patient takes one of two paths after diagnosis. Tracking each patient’s chronic condition count from 2021 to 2024 and projecting one additional year, the divergence between those who improve and those who don’t is striking, and it compounds over time.

Why This Model Uses $1,000 as the Average Employer Savings / Member

Two different weighted-average savings figures sit behind this number, because the Ring-Enabled and Device-Agnostic layers reach different populations.

The $1,053.22 figure is weighted using the diagnosed, uncontrolled care-gap mix, which matches the narrower population the Ring-Enabled layer actually reaches. The Device-Agnostic layer casts a wider net across the full care-gap population, both diagnosed and undiagnosed members, so its condition mix is different and produces a lower weighted average of $944.33. Rather than carry two separate rates through the model, this version uses $1,000, the approximate midpoint of the two, as a single simplified employer-savings-per-member figure for both layers.

Important takeaway: if Oura is paying for the ring, sleep apnea alone does not economically support the hardware at these assumptions—the $13–15K revenue ceiling sits well below the ~$40–50K net hardware cost. The ring economics need to be spread across multiple conditions and a broader eligible cohort, while Counsel / site-of-care value sits in the broader device-agnostic employer layer.

Competitive Landscape Deep Dive · Care Navigation

Care Navigation Is Consolidating Fast, and AI Is Deciding Who Wins the Next Employer Renewal

Market definition: Sizing includes benefits and plan navigation, clinical case management, carve-out physician-led navigation, and Centers of Excellence steering, sized at $3.83B (US, 2025) growing to $6.21B by 2031 at an 8.40% CAGR, per Precedence Research’s Healthcare Navigation Platform Market report (see footnote).

How AI Is Disrupting the Market

AI now runs core coordination and triage work, not just chat support in the background.

How AI Is Disrupting the Market

Quantum Health’s Warrior Assist and Transcarent’s WayFinding platform use AI to automate care-coordinator workflows. Rightway’s Curai Health partnership (Nov 2024) lets AI triage members directly inside the navigation flow instead of referring them to a separate telehealth vendor.

New Entrants & Innovators

Consolidation, not new entrants, is reshaping who competes in this market.

New Entrants & Innovators

Transcarent acquired Accolade for $621M (Apr 2025). Quantum Health acquired Embold Health and CirrusMD in 2025. Personify Health formed from the Virgin Pulse and HealthComp merger (Feb 2024). Three or four full-stack platforms are emerging from what used to be a fragmented field.

Where VC Money Is Flowing

Investors are placing fewer, larger bets on proven platforms rather than funding new entrants.

Where VC Money Is Flowing

Care navigation held just 12.5% of digital health VC deals but captured 24.3% of the dollars over the past year, a 1.95x capital-to-deal ratio. Rightway’s $155M raise in September 2026 is a recent example of this large, late-stage pattern.

Headwinds
  • Employer satisfaction with standalone navigation is mixed
  • Consolidation is shrinking the number of independent platforms to choose from
  • Carriers bundling “good enough” navigation into their fees undercuts standalone vendors
Additional Context

Mercer’s 2025 survey found only about 46% of employers with a carve-out advocacy or navigation program report being satisfied with its performance, even though 20% of large employers now run one.

Tailwinds
  • Employers want to extend navigation to a broader, lower-cost-to-serve population, not just complex cases
  • GLP-1 and specialty drug cost surge is a fresh source of demand for navigation-led steering
  • AI is lowering cost-to-serve, making navigation economics work at broader population scale
Additional Context

Nearly half of large employers now cover GLP-1 drugs for obesity, up from 44% in 2024, a fast-growing source of employer interest in navigation-led utilization management (Mercer 2025).

Regulatory / Structural Barriers to Entry
  • Employers renew benefits once a year, so vendors get one shot per prospect
  • Carve-outs only work for self-funded plans, capping the base near 100M lives
  • Accreditation and clinical licensing slow down new entrants
Additional Context

Carve-out navigation is only available to self-funded (ERISA) employers, which caps the addressable base at roughly 100 to 105 million covered lives, and most employers only evaluate vendors once a year during open enrollment.

Competitive Landscape Deep Dive · Digital Chronic Care

Chronic Care Has Gone Public, and GLP-1 Companion Programs Are the New Growth Engine

Market definition: Sizing includes condition-specific coaching and connected-device platforms for diabetes, hypertension, obesity/weight management, and musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions, sized at $1.98B (US, 2025) growing to $4.26B by 2031 at a 13.64% CAGR, per Precedence Research’s US Chronic Disease Management Market report (see footnote).

How AI Is Disrupting the Market

AI has become the primary interface for coaching and care delivery, not just a support tool.

How AI Is Disrupting the Market

Omada’s OmadaSpark agent (launched May 2025) delivers real-time motivational interviewing. Virta credits AI automation of patient interactions for its roughly 60% gross margin. Hinge Health pairs AI motion tracking with its FDA-cleared Enso wearable to automate physical therapy.

New Entrants & Innovators

The category had its long-awaited IPO breakout in 2025.

New Entrants & Innovators

Omada Health and Hinge Health both went public in 2025, the first digital health IPOs since 2021, and both beat Wall Street growth expectations in their first quarters as public companies.

Where VC Money Is Flowing

Digital health VC funding rebounded sharply, with AI and chronic care as the biggest draws.

Where VC Money Is Flowing

Digital health VC funding hit $14.2B in 2025, up 35% year over year, with AI-enabled startups capturing 54% of the dollars, up from 37% in 2024. Chronic care was named a top category for large deals heading into 2026.

Headwinds
  • Post-IPO public scrutiny raises the bar on unit economics and profitability timelines
  • Point-solution fatigue is pushing employers toward multi-condition platforms, disadvantaging single-condition players
  • GLP-1 cost pressure could push employers to restrict drug access rather than pay for companion coaching
Additional Context

Point-solution fatigue is pushing employers toward multi-condition platforms. Omada notes that 31% of its clients already use two or more of its programs, a trend that disadvantages single-condition competitors.

Tailwinds
  • GLP-1 companion and support programs are the primary 2025 growth driver cited by Omada and Virta
  • Employers are consolidating point solutions into single multi-condition vendors, benefiting platform players
  • Two successful 2025 IPOs are re-opening capital markets access for the category
Additional Context

Omada’s GLP-1 Enhanced Care Track and Virta’s GLP-1 companion programs were both cited by management as the primary driver of 2025 membership and revenue growth.

Regulatory / Structural Barriers to Entry
  • Connected devices need FDA clearance, adding time before launch
  • Published clinical results are now expected to win an RFP
  • Major PBM partnerships are a gatekeeper new entrants must also secure
Additional Context

Hinge Health’s Enso device required FDA clearance before launch, and RFPs increasingly expect published, peer-reviewed outcomes data, a bar that newer, unproven entrants struggle to clear.

Competitive Landscape Deep Dive · Telehealth (Employer Benefit)

Employer Telehealth Growth Has Slowed to Single Digits as the Category Matures

Market definition: Sizing is scoped to visit-based virtual urgent, primary, and behavioral care sold through employer and health-plan benefit channels, derived from Teladoc’s disclosed US Integrated Care segment revenue ($1.58B, 2025), not the broader “total US telehealth market” figures that include hospital telemedicine and international/DTC categories out of scope here (see footnote).

How AI Is Disrupting the Market

Vendors are repositioning around AI and software instead of pay-per-visit revenue.

How AI Is Disrupting the Market

Amwell’s subscription and software revenue grew even as its total revenue declined in 2025, reflecting a shift toward AI-enabled infrastructure licensing. Rightway now handles AI triage in-house through its Curai Health partnership rather than buying pure-play telehealth.

New Entrants & Innovators

Players are repositioning into new niches rather than launching head-on competitors.

New Entrants & Innovators

Lyra Health acquired Bend Health in July 2025 to expand into pediatric behavioral care instead of competing directly for adult behavioral telehealth market share.

Where VC Money Is Flowing

Investors are rotating away from pure visit-based telehealth toward AI-native and chronic-care models instead.

Where VC Money Is Flowing

Virtual care platforms drew only about $373M across 7 deals over the past year, a much smaller pool than care navigation or chronic care attracted in the same period.

Headwinds
  • Growth has decelerated to low-single-digits as employer telehealth penetration matures
  • DTC/cash-pay behavioral telehealth is shrinking (BetterHelp -9% FY2025) as insurance-based options undercut pricing
  • Amwell’s decline reflects broader pressure on pure visit-based, per-visit telehealth models
Additional Context

Teladoc’s BetterHelp segment, its cash-pay behavioral telehealth business, declined 9% in FY2025 as insurance-based competitors undercut its pricing.

Tailwinds
  • AI-enabled triage is lowering the cost-to-serve for virtual urgent and behavioral care
  • Insurance-covered behavioral telehealth demand is rising; Teladoc is expanding BetterHelp’s insurance acceptance to all 50 states
  • Bundling telehealth into navigation/chronic-care platforms is a growth path even as standalone growth slows
Additional Context

Teladoc has expanded BetterHelp’s insurance acceptance to all 50 states and grown its credentialed provider base from about 6,000 to more than 8,000 to meet rising insurance-based demand.

Regulatory / Structural Barriers to Entry
  • State-by-state licensing limits how fast a vendor can scale nationally
  • Controlled-substance prescribing rules create uncertainty, especially for psychiatry
  • Most carriers already include some telehealth benefit for free, raising the bar to prove extra value
Additional Context

Multi-state medical licensure and DEA controlled-substance prescribing rules are especially limiting for psychiatry and behavioral telehealth, where prescribing volume is highest.

How the 3.0x Employer ROI Is Calculated

Employer ROI is always 3.0x by construction: the Revenue Pool available to Oura is set at Employer Value divided by 3, so Employer Value divided by the Revenue Pool always resolves to exactly 3.0x, regardless of the underlying inputs.

Employer Value ÷ Revenue Pool (Employer Value ÷ 3) = 3.0x Employer ROI, for every employer.

This 3:1 relationship holds for both the Ring-Enabled and Device-Agnostic layers on this page. Oura’s actual revenue is then its negotiated share of that Revenue Pool, which varies by layer and scenario.
